pr_title: Fix regression with absolute path includes when OPENSSL_CONF_INCLUDE is set
pr_body:
Do not prepend $OPENSSL_CONF_INCLUDE to absolute include paths
    
Also check for malloc failure and do not add '/' when
$OPENSSL_CONF_INCLUDE already ends with directory separator.

Fixes #13302

issue_context.title: Absolute paths in a .include directive no longer working with master
issue_context.body:
I have numerous times seen or been bitten myself by an attempt to ".include" a file which is specified with an absolute path. Unfortunately this only works with relative paths.

I can't think of a good reason to disallow absolute paths. Should we add this? I think it would be a significant usability improvement.

See for example:

https://mta.openssl.org/pipermail/openssl-users/2020-November/013105.html
comments: I am confused - why shouldn't the `.include` directive already support absolute paths? If this does not work, it must be a regression. It works fine with 1.1.1.

> I am confused - why shouldn't the .include directive already support absolute paths? If this does not work, it must be a regression. It works fine with 1.1.1.

I haven't looked into why it doesn't work. I've only observed that if you provide one then it fails.
At some point, we should have an internal platform agnostic path editing library.  A bit like perl's File::Spec.

review_comments:
On VMS, `[foo]` is an absolute path, while `[.foo]` and `[-.foo]` aren't.

File::Spec::VMS has a nearly readable regexp for it: https://metacpan.org/release/PathTools/source/lib/File/Spec/VMS.pm#L340
Essentially, what that says is that if *the first* `<` or a `[` you find *is not* followed by a `.`, a `-`, a `]`, or a `>`, it's an absolute path.
(`<` and `>` can be used instead of `[` and `]` as directory delimiters on VMS...  that's legacy coming all the way from TOPS-20, maybe even TOPS-10 (I've forgotten))
So we consider something an absolute path if it starts with `/` even on VMS and WIN32? Is that correct behaviour?
I think it is correct on WIN32. Not sure about VMS. @levitte ?
@mattcaswell Actually according to https://metacpan.org/release/PathTools/source/lib/File/Spec/VMS.pm#L339 also on VMS `/` on beginning marks an absolute path.
